result:
I saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. When I ran the same code on Q2, every one of the 10 reference values matched exactly.

**Q3 results (paid orders only)**

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | enterprise, 308,738,043 KRW |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 243 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | svc, 399,933,245 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u217@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 230 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 703,476 KRW |
| h. August → September growth | -16.3% |

The data had three issues that the definitions don't settle. I picked the option that reproduced the Q2 values each time:

- **Time zone:** order times are stored in UTC (ending in `Z`). Quarters and months are cut on Korean time (UTC+9). With UTC cutoffs, the Q2 values for a, c, g and h don't match.
- **Counting customers:** some customer IDs share the same email, so I treated one email as one customer. Counting by ID gives 274 and 217 for Q2 b and f instead of 228 and 190.
- **Segment names:** spellings were inconsistent (`'SMB'`, `' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '`, etc.), so I lowercased them and trimmed spaces before grouping.

Answer a depends on the time zone. Cutting on UTC would give smb at 313,075,390 KRW instead of enterprise.

The analysis script is at `/tmp/s/a.py`.
